Design spec for the home screen and the visual system it establishes. Source of truth for implementation; the interactive version lives in the Omelette project `Macros Tracker Native setup` as `Macros Tracker App.dc.html` (option **4a**), where every state below is clickable.

Direction: athletic / performance — bold numerals, high contrast, near-zero chrome. Reference point is gym and wearable instrumentation, not a consumer food app.

## Tokens

### Colour

| Role | Hex | Notes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Background | `#000000` | True black. No gradients except the scrim below |
| Surface | `#0E1013` | Cards, tiles, sheets |
| Chip / track | `#1B1E23` | Progress track, calendar cell, secondary button |
| Ring track | `#17191D` | Ring background stroke only |
| Hairline | `rgba(255,255,255,0.09)` | 1px borders, list separators |
| Text | `#FFFFFF` | Primary |
| Text dim | `#8B8F98` | Labels, metadata, body copy |
| Text muted | `#4A4E55` | Disabled, unlogged calendar days |
| **Accent** | `#5EE7E0` | Calories, every primary action, active states |
| On-accent | `#00201E` | Text/icon on an accent fill |
| Protein | `#7BEBA4` | Only when the goal is cleared |
| Fiber | `#B79CFF` | Only when the goal is cleared |
| Over target | `#FFA24D` | Calories only. See semantics below |
| Over-target fill | `#FFA24D` at 10% | Nudge card background |
| Over-target border | `#FFA24D` at 28% | Nudge card border |

**Colour semantics — this is the load-bearing rule.** Over target means opposite things per macro. Calories over target is orange and phrased as a nudge. Protein and fiber over target are *good* — they turn to their own colour with the label `goal cleared`, never orange, never a warning. Under target for protein/fiber is plain white with `Ng to go`. Orange appears nowhere else in the app.

### Type

Two families, both Google Fonts.

* **Archivo** — all UI text. Weights 600 / 700 / 800 / 900. Numerals always 900 with `letter-spacing: -0.03em` to `-0.05em` and `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
* **IBM Plex Mono** — every label, unit, timestamp and metric string. Uppercase, `letter-spacing` 0.08em–0.18em, sizes 9–13px.

| Element | Size / weight |
| -- | -- |
| Ring numeral | 52px / 900 |
| Date title | 27px / 800 |
| Tile numeral | 27px / 900 |
| Section title (sheets) | 20px / 800 |
| Entry name | 14px / 600 |
| Body copy | 13–14px / 400, `line-height: 1.5`, `text-wrap: pretty` |
| Mono label | 10px / 500, `letter-spacing: 0.16em` |

### Geometry

Tight variant — chosen over two looser options.

* Corner radius: 10px cards and buttons, 6px thumbnails, 8px calendar cells, 999px dots only
* Ring: `r=100` in a 240 viewBox, **12px stroke**, `stroke-linecap: butt`, rotated −90°, max rendered size 222px
* Screen padding: 18px horizontal, 58px top (under the status bar), 132px bottom (clears the log button)
* Vertical rhythm: 16px between major blocks, 8px between paired tiles
* Progress bars: 4px tall, square ends, no radius
* Minimum hit target 44px — the date title, entry rows, calendar cells and both buttons all clear it

## Home screen

Vertical order, top to bottom:

1. **Date title + streak** — `Today ▾` (or the weekday name for past days) with the date beneath in mono. The whole title block is the tap target for the date picker. Streak pill sits right: accent dot, count, `DAYS`
2. **Calorie ring** — the hero. Centre stack is `REMAINING` / big numeral / `KCAL LEFT` / `1690 of 2350 kcal`. Over target the same stack becomes `PAST TARGET` / overage / `KCAL OVER`, ring fills 100% in orange
3. **Protein and fiber tiles** — equal-width pair. Mono label, numeral, `/target g`, 4px bar, status line
4. **Nudge card** — only when calories are over. See below
5. **What should I eat?** — full-width, surface fill, accent hairline border. Right side carries the remaining budget in mono (`660 · 57P LEFT`). Both strings are `white-space: nowrap`
6. **Entry list** — mono heading with the count, then rows separated by hairlines, newest first
7. **Log food** — fixed to the bottom over a `linear-gradient(to top, #000 46%, transparent)` scrim so the list scrolls under it legibly. Full-width accent fill, mono uppercase

### Entry row

40px thumbnail (6px radius) · name (single line, ellipsis) · mono meta `08:14 · 41P · 6F` · calories right-aligned in mono. Tapping expands in place: the AI note, then `EDIT` / `RE-ANALYZE` / `DELETE` as mono accent links, indented to the text column. `RE-ANALYZE` is the re-prompt path from plan doc 06; `EDIT` is the inline path. Both must exist.

Entries with no photo get a flat `#1B1E23` block, not a placeholder icon.

### The nudge card

Fires only when calories exceed target. Two lines: a mono tag stating the overage in non-judgemental terms, then one sentence naming the lowest protein-per-calorie entry of the day and a concrete alternative.

Live copy:

> `160 KCAL OVER — NOT A BIG DEAL`
> The bagel breakfast returned the least protein per calorie today. Eggs on the same rye would have covered the gap for about half the calories.

Computation is deterministic — rank the day's entries by `protein_g / calories` ascending and name the lowest. No AI call needed for this, which means it can ship with E5 rather than waiting for E11. The AI coaching layer in plan doc 11 then extends the same slot rather than introducing a new one.

**Tone rule: nudge, never scold.** No red, no exclamation marks, no streak-loss language, no implication of failure.

### Empty day

Dashed hairline container: mono `NO ENTRIES`, `Nothing logged this day`, one line of body copy, and an `Add from library` accent button — for a past day the camera is the wrong first offer.

## Date navigation

Chosen pattern: **tap the date title → month calendar sheet.**

* Sheet slides from the bottom (`260ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)`), accent 2px top border, dimmed backdrop that closes on tap
* Three weeks of cells, Sunday-start, fixed weekday header row
* **Logged days** — `#1B1E23` fill, white numeral, accent dot. **Unlogged days** — `#0E1013` fill, muted numeral, no dot, not tappable. **Selected day** — accent fill, dark numeral
* The grid therefore doubles as a consistency map; a run of flat cells is a visible gap
* `JUMP TO TODAY` button pinned at the bottom of the sheet

Selecting a day resets the expanded entry and closes any open sheet.

**Known cost, still open:** this makes "yesterday" a two-tap job, and yesterday is the common case. Recommend adding horizontal swipe on the day content for adjacent days on top of this, keeping the calendar for arbitrary jumps. Not yet designed.

## Advice sheet

Same sheet chrome as the calendar. Header `Three that fit`, then the remaining budget in mono, then exactly three cards: name, macros in accent mono, one line on why it fits. Three is deliberate — one reads arbitrary, five is a menu.

Server assembles all context; the client sends nothing but the request. See plan doc 08.

## Decisions this design forces

1. **Does an empty day break the streak?** The build computes the streak from `DailyLog` rows with at least one entry and stops at the first gap, so Jul 28 with no entries drops the streak from 9 to 4. Doc 07 lists this as open. The screen shows the strict reading; if a "rest day" concept is wanted, it has to be modelled, not implied
2. **Today counts before you log.** The streak holds through today until the day ends — per doc 07's recommendation
3. **Remaining, not consumed, is the hero.** Consumed is available as the secondary `1690 of 2350` line. Every screen decision follows from remaining being the actionable number
4. **Protein gets tile parity with calories**, not third billing. It is the target people actually chase

## Screens still to design

Welcome / sign in · onboarding question flow · targets result and adjust · capture → review → correct · entry detail and edit · settings · post-day recap (E11).

## Rejected along the way

* **Scoreboard layout** — calories and protein as two enormous numerals, no ring. Read well, but lost the at-a-glance sense of proportion the ring gives
* **Photo-forward cards** — entries as large plates with the numbers underneath. Handsome, and wrong: the numbers are why the screen exists
* **Week strip** — five day chips above the ring. Cost ~70px of vertical space and dead-ended at five days with no route to last month
* **Acid palette** (lime on true black) and **Ice** (periwinkle on blue-black). Cyan held the athletic read without the lime's harshness
* **Jade accent** — collides with the green that already means `goal cleared`
* **Warm accents** (magenta, hi-vis yellow) — force the over-target warning off orange

## Amendment — 1 Aug 2026 (design review)

1. Header gains a `≡` **button** beside the streak chip, opening the menu specified in doc 19. It is the only new affordance on the home screen. Tapping the streak chip pushes the Streak screen (doc 20).
2. **Over-target ring rule.** Approved 1 Aug. When intake exceeds the calorie target the outer ring renders **full** in the warning colour `#FFA24D` — the budget is spent, and a full ring is the honest reading of that. The overage is drawn as a **separate inner arc at r=76, stroke 8** (outer ring is r=100, stroke 12), on the same target scale, starting at 12 o'clock and running clockwise. 310 kcal over a 2,350 target therefore sweeps 13.2% of the inner circle — it reads as a fraction of a day rather than as a second lap, which is the proportion information the previous treatment destroyed.

   The centre numeral flips from *remaining* to *overage*: caption `OVER BY`, numeral `310` at 52px in the warning colour, unit `KCAL`, and the raw ratio `2,660 / 2,350` beneath in dim mono. Protein and fiber tiles are unaffected and keep their own colours — being over on calories does not mean the day failed, and the tiles are where that nuance lives.

   Rendered as `8d` in the design file; exported to `exports/shell-8d-over-target.png`.
3. **Minimum type size.** No text below **11px** anywhere in the app. Every 9px and 10px mono label across all screens has been raised to 11–11.5px. Mono caps carry ≥0.06em tracking at those sizes.
4. **Date navigation is unchanged.** The calendar picker stays as the only way to move between days; swipe-between-days was considered and deferred pending TestFlight feedback.
